knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: Xi chain
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. In a generalised linear model, what is the role of link function g?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: The link connects the response mean scale to the systematic component.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: The link satisfies g(E[Y|X]) = X beta.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Treating the link as a transformation that makes the raw response Normal.

choices.label: It maps conditional mean mu to the linear predictor through g(mu) = eta = X beta.
It maps each residual directly to a probability density.
It forces every response distribution to become Normal.
It specifies covariance between all observations.

knowledge_checks.title: Revision Checkpoint: GLM deviance and model choice
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Two nested GLMs use the same response family and scale treatment. What is a valid use of their deviance difference?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: For appropriate nested GLMs, deviance difference is a likelihood-ratio statistic, often asymptotically chi-squared.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Use the deviance difference for a nested-model test while retaining residual checks.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Automatically choosing complexity or treating one test as complete validation.

choices.label: Under suitable regularity conditions, it can test whether added terms improve fit using an asymptotic chi-squared reference.
The model with more parameters must be chosen because its deviance cannot increase.
A deviance difference is always compared with standard Normal.
A non-significant difference proves every residual assumption.
